what_happened: The ego was going straight in its lane at about 8 m/s, roughly 20 m behind where the human drove, while log-replayed cars passed it on the right. Actor 24 moved left from the right lane into the ego's lane (about 1 m of lateral shift between 8.2 s and 9.2 s) and its side met the ego's front-right corner, which counts as a front collision. The ego itself moved only about 0.5 m off the recorded path.

On a straight highway, the ego slowed from 8.7 to 7.0 m/s in its lane while vehicles came up from behind on the right; actor 14 passed and cut in about 10 m ahead, then actor 24 came alongside and leaned across the lane line into the ego's front-right corner. The ego was only 0.4 m off the recorded human path, and its planned path and heading tilted slightly right, so it may have helped close the gap. It's unclear whether the policy or actor 24 was mostly to blame.

On a multi-lane arterial with the command changing to RIGHT, the ego sped up from 2.5 to 5.9 m/s. Instead of following its planned path to the right, it yawed and drifted about 2 m left of the recorded trajectory, onto the left lane line. There it made side contact with actor 56, which was coming up in the adjacent left lane just behind it; 56 also struck the ego's rear.

The ego was following slow car 48 on a multi-lane highway at about 4 m/s. Instead of following its route, which bore right (command RIGHT), it steered left toward the next lane and its side hit car 7, which was coming up from behind in that lane. The ego was about 2 m off the recorded path at impact, and car 7 also made contact with the ego's rear.

On the multi-lane highway, the ego crept left out of its lane behind the slow white car (48), ending up about 1.9 m left of the recorded path. Its side then hit car 7, which was coming up from behind in the left adjacent lane (lateral collision at 8.2 s). The route command was RIGHT and the planned path pointed right, but the ego's actual motion kept drifting left.

The ego was going straight in its lane on a highway at about 8 m/s and stayed within 0.45 m of the human's path. Actor 24 came up from the right rear and cut left across the lane line into the ego's front-right corner, which counted as a front collision at 9.2 s. The ego was about 20 m behind where the human was at that time, so the replayed actor merged into space the human had already cleared.

After handoff, the ego sped up from 2.5 to 6 m/s. It steered left into the next lane, while the recorded human path and the RIGHT command went straight or right. At 7.7 s it made side contact with actor 56, which was driving alongside and slightly behind it in that lane. No vehicle was close ahead, so this was a bad lane change by the ego, not a failure to brake.

On a straight multi-lane highway with no lead vehicle within about 45 m, the policy braked hard for no clear reason (23.7 to 7.4 m/s) and drifted left toward the lane line. Actor 1, which had been behind on the left, came up alongside, and the ego's front-left corner struck it.

After handoff the ego braked hard on an open highway, from 22 to 6.4 m/s, with no lead within about 45–50 m, and fell 13.5 m behind its recorded position. Actor 1, a replayed vehicle from the lane to the left that expected the ego to be further ahead, drew level and cut into the ego's lane just in front, so the ego's front struck it; the ego was also rear-ended by traffic behind.

The ego kept straight in its lane on a multi-lane arterial, within 0.3 m of the recorded path, but eased off from 9.8 to 8.3 m/s, so by 7.7 s it was about 8 m behind where the human was at that time. Actor 14 came up from behind on the right and passed the ego. Its replayed path then merged into the ego's lane, into the space the logged car had already left, and it hit the ego's front-right corner. The ego could not have avoided this.

On the highway behind lead car 48, the ego steered left out of its lane (orange path), away from the recorded route, which went straight and then RIGHT. It sideswiped actor 7, which was coming up from behind in the left lane (lateral collision at 8.2 s).

On a multi-lane highway, the ego sped up from 2.5 to 6 m/s and drifted about 2 m to the side of the recorded human path, into the edge of the neighboring lane. There it made side contact with actor 56, which was alongside and just behind it (lateral collision, with rear contact also recorded); the cars ahead were never close.

The ego was going straight in its freeway lane at about 8 m/s, within 0.4 m of the recorded path laterally. Actor 24 came up from behind in the lane to the right and moved left across the lane line, so its rear clipped the ego's front-right corner. The ego was about 20 m behind where the human car was at that moment (the faint box ahead on the map). The other car is a replay of the real drive, so it cut into a gap that held the human car but now held the ego.

On an open highway, with the nearest vehicle ahead about 45–50 m away, the ego braked hard for no visible reason (23.7 to 7.5 m/s) and drifted left toward the lane line. Actor 1, coming up in the left lane from behind, drew alongside, and the ego's front-left clipped it. This counts as an at-fault front collision; the ego was also rear-ended at some point.

The ego was going straight at about 8 m/s in its lane when actor 24 came up from behind in the lane to its right, passed it, and closed in on its front-right corner, clipping it at 9.2 s. The ego had drifted only about 0.65 m right of the recorded human path, so the contact mostly comes from the replayed actor sweeping across the lane line, with a small contribution from the ego's rightward drift.

On the freeway, the recorded human driver moved right toward car 48's lane. The ego instead held its lane at about 4–5 m/s, with its plan bending slightly left. Car 7 came from behind-left and drifted right into the space the human had left, so it hit the ego's left rear side at 8.2 s, which is a lateral contact that also counts as being rear-ended.

On a multi-lane road with a RIGHT command, the ego sped up from 2.5 to 5.7 m/s and drifted about 2 m to the left of the recorded human path, across the lane line. Its side hit actor 56, which was travelling alongside on the left-rear in the next lane, so the result was a lateral collision rather than a lead-vehicle impact.
